Occupational Health

Occupational health — pre-placement checks, hazards, compensation, ESI, occupational diseases and prevention.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe occupational health care
  • List workplace hazards
  • Explain occupational diseases
  • Differentiate compensation schemes

In simple words

Occupational health protects the health of workers and promotes their productivity. It looks at hazards, prevention, early detection, treatment, rehabilitation and compensation.

Objectives of occupational health

  • Prevent work-related injury and disease
  • Detect and treat occupational disease early
  • Adjust workers to their work where possible
  • Improve the work environment
  • Provide first aid, emergency plans and rehabilitation
  • Advocate for laws, compensation and welfare services

Workplace hazards

Hazard Examples Diseases
Dust Silica, coal, cotton Silicosis, coal worker’s pneumoconiosis, byssinosis
Chemicals Lead, mercury, solvents, asbestos Anaemia, dermatitis, asbestosis
Noise Machinery, blasting Noise-induced hearing loss
Heat Furnaces, mining Heat stress
Radiation Nuclear, X-ray Cancer, genetic damage
Physical Falls, machinery Injuries

Workers’ health services

  • Pre-placement examination — protects workers from unsuitable jobs
  • Periodic medical examinations — early detection
  • Emergency and first aid services — first aid boxes, trained staff
  • Health education — nutrition, hygiene, HIV and tobacco
  • Welfare measures — drinking water, toilets, canteen, housing, rest, crèche
  • Mental health — stress, work-life balance, counselling

Compensation and legislation

  • Employee’s State Insurance (ESI) Act, 1948 — medical care and cash benefit for workers
  • Factories Act, 1948 — working conditions, safety, welfare
  • Workmen’s / Employees’ Compensation Act — payment for injury or death
  • Mines Act — working conditions in mines
  • Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 — consolidated safety rules

🔴 Worker health affects everyone

Occupational disease returns to the family and to the community. Prevention at the workplace, early detection and immediate reporting are cheaper than treatment and compensation.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Occupational health covers prevention and treatment of work-related illness and injury.
  2. Silicosis is caused by exposure to silica dust.
  3. Byssinosis affects cotton textile workers.
  4. Pre-placement examination prevents workers from unsuitable jobs.
  5. The ESI Act of 1948 provides medical and cash benefits for workers.
  6. Hazards include dust, chemicals, noise, heat and radiation.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Periodic examinations detect occupational disease early.
  2. Employees Compensation Act provides compensation for injury or death.
  3. Factories Act regulates safety and welfare conditions.
  4. Noise exposure causes sensorineural hearing loss.
  5. Occupational health includes mental wellbeing at work.

📌 Memory trick

Occupational diseases: dust workers get pneumoconiosis.

60-second revision

  • Occupational health: prevent, protect, detect, treat, rehabilitate.
  • Hazards: dust, chemicals, noise, heat, radiation.
  • Diseases: silicosis, pneumoconiosis, asbestosis, byssinosis.
  • Worker services: pre-placement checks, periodic exams, first aid, welfare.
  • Laws: ESI 1948, Factories Act 1948, Employees’ Compensation Act.

Test yourself

Silicosis is caused by exposure to:

Answer: B. Long exposure to silica dust causes silicosis, a fibrotic lung disease.

Byssinosis affects:

Answer: B. Byssinosis is an airway disease among workers exposed to cotton dust.

Pre-placement examination is used to:

Answer: B. Pre-placement checks prevent a worker from taking a job that could damage health.

The ESI Act was passed in:

Answer: A. The Employees State Insurance Act, 1948 provides medical care and cash benefits for workers.

Which protects workers from noise exposure?

Answer: B. Ear plugs and ear muffs prevent noise-induced hearing loss.
